title: USRP-2940 Specifications
reviewed_scope: Targeted extracted text of specifications; not a visual page-by-page review
claims: 40 MHz and 120 MHz options exist
120 MHz option: maximum instantaneous bandwidth 120 MHz; maximum I/Q sample rate 200 MS/s; ADC resolution 14 bit
2 RX, 50 MHz–2.2 GHz; DRAM 1024 MB
limitations: Actual user unit variant and usable bandwidth not measured; DRAM specification does not establish API buffering behavior.

title: NI Ettus USRP Software Defined Radios Product Brochure
claims: USRP-2940 maps to X310 + WBX, 40/120 MHz options
limitations: Family mapping; inspect installed daughterboard variant rather than inferring it solely from chassis name.

title: About USRP Bandwidths and Sampling Rates
locators: How do I calculate the bandwidth of my USRP-based system?
claims: Analog, FPGA and host bandwidth are separate constraints
WBX-120 analog bandwidth is 120 MHz; WBX is 40 MHz
16-bit I/Q interface table gives X300/X310 200 MS/s for 10GbE and 4-lane PCIe as theoretical maxima
limitations: Host performance depends on implementation. Do not generalize table throughput to current PC, disk or software path.

title: USRP X3x0 Series
locators: Addressing the Device > Single device configuration
claims: Default master clock 200 MHz; 184.32 MHz also supported
Stock application IQ rates derive from supported integer divisions; requested sample rates may be coerced
Master clock is configured at initialization, not freely changed while the device remains initialized
limitations: This is UHD behavior; NI custom FPGA images may implement different host interfaces. Actual returned rates must be recorded.

title: Device Synchronization
locators: Synchronizing Channel Phase > Align CORDICs in the DSP
Align LOs in the front-end (SBX, UBX, OBX)
claims: 10 MHz establishes common frequency reference; PPS synchronizes device sample time
Timed stream commands align digital CORDIC start
Frontends outside listed timed-retune exceptions may acquire random LO phase offsets on tuning, requiring phase realignment
limitations: WBX is not listed among SBX/UBX/OBX deterministic-retune exceptions. Receiver time synchronization does not lock smartphone display clocks.

title: What is the Difference Between Sample Rate and I/Q Rate on NI RF Devices?
claims: Hardware ADC sampling and decimated application I/Q rates are distinct
0.8 times I/Q rate is a filter-rolloff programming guideline
Inadequate host transfer causes overflow/lost buffered data
limitations: 0.8 factor is a general guideline, not measured RF passband or a claim that arbitrary application Fs is supported.

title: USRP-2940/2942/2943/2944/2945 Getting Started Guide
locators: pp.8–10 Programming the USRP RIO / NI-USRP Instrument Driver / Sample Projects / Examples
reviewed_scope: Targeted software and connector sections; not all 34 pages read
claims: USRP-2940R is covered by the NI-USRP/RIO programming guide
NI-USRP instrument-driver examples and LabVIEW FPGA customization are distinct workflows
Back panel offers 1G/10G Ethernet, PCIe x4 MXI, REF and PPS connections
limitations: Older guide; confirm current installed driver/FPGA/LabVIEW combination before changing software or hardware.

title: NI-USRP 20.0 Readme
claims: Explicitly lists USRP-2940 40 MHz and 120 MHz variants
Lists WBX and WBX-120 daughterboard support
Lists LabVIEW versions supported by this historical driver release
limitations: Not a recommendation to install version20.0 or proof that all current LabVIEW versions work with this driver.

title: Supported Radio Devices
locators: Supported FPGA Image Flavors and Network Interfaces
reviewed_scope: Relevant feature, interface and daughterboard tables
claims: Wireless Testbench R2026b uses UHD4.9.0.0
X310 WBX daughterboards support live data I/O using SDRu System objects/blocks
WBX does not inherit UBX160/TwinRX baseband capture workflow support
Documented MATLAB X3xx interface excludes PCIe
limitations: Actual installed Wireless Testbench/license/support package and matching radio FPGA image not inspected in this research task.

title: comm.SDRuReceiver: Receive data from USRP device
locators: Get Radio Information for Multichannel Radio
Burst Mode Buffering With SDRu Receiver
claims: Uses UHD over Ethernet for supported X3xx radios
info reports device and rate configuration
len and overrun outputs must be checked for valid contiguous data
Burst buffering exists but is not a blanket continuity guarantee between bursts
limitations: No runtime API or hardware test performed. Example metadata or IP addresses are not the user's configuration.

title: ni/labview-usrp-examples README
claims: Examples require LabVIEW2025Q3+, Python3.10/3.12 and UHD/PythonAPI4.8+
NI-USRP driver is not required for these examples
README reports only a few MS/s for host-to-USRP LabVIEW IQ streaming
limitations: Not an established 200MS/s path; do not replace an existing working acquisition chain solely based on this repository.
